bio.en: Born in Virginia, he was president of Princeton University and governor of New Jersey before winning the presidency in 1912, and in his first year imposed racial segregation across the federal bureaucracy. In April 1917 he asked Congress to declare war over unrestricted submarine warfare, and in January 1918 set out the Fourteen Points, with a League of Nations and self-determination. At the Paris Peace Conference he presided over the drafting of the League Covenant but conceded much to the other powers to get it. A stroke in October 1919 incapacitated him, and his refusal of a compromise sank the Senate’s ratification of the treaty. The Palmer Raids of the Red Scare came in the same years. He received the 1919 Nobel Peace Prize and died in 1924.

bio.en: Born in Manchester to Welsh parents, he made his name as a radical Liberal orator. As chancellor of the exchequer he introduced the 1909 People’s Budget and the National Insurance Act, laying foundations of the welfare state. After serving as minister of munitions and secretary for war he became prime minister in December 1916. At the Paris Peace Conference he opposed reparations that would wreck the German economy and sought to check French dominance. In 1921 he concluded the Anglo-Soviet Trade Agreement and negotiated the creation of the Irish Free State, but resigned in 1922 when the Conservatives left the coalition. In 1936 he met Hitler and praised him. He died in 1945.

bio.en: Born in Palermo, he became a renowned law professor and from 1897 sat in the Chamber of Deputies as a Liberal. When the government fell after the defeat at Caporetto in October 1917 he became prime minister, dismissed Cadorna and rebuilt the army, and the victory of Vittorio Veneto in 1918 earned him the name “Premier of Victory”. At the peace conference he demanded Dalmatia, promised by the Treaty of London, and Fiume, obtained neither, walked out in April 1919 and resigned in June. The “mutilated victory” helped Mussolini’s rise. He at first supported Mussolini but broke with him after the murder of Matteotti in 1924. He died in Rome in 1952.

bio.en: Born to an ethnic German farming family in Moravia, he studied law in Vienna, joined the Social Democrats and entered the Imperial Council in 1907. An Austromarxist theorist of “personal autonomy” on the national question, he was criticised by Lenin and Stalin. In 1918 he became the first chancellor of German-Austria, leading a grand coalition that introduced the eight-hour day among other reforms, and had to accept the ban on union with Germany and the territorial losses of Saint-Germain. He supported the Anschluss in 1938. In April 1945, at Soviet direction, he formed a provisional government, and that year became president. He died in Vienna in 1950.

bio.en: Born in Berlin, he entered the Reichstag for the National Liberals in 1907 and during the war backed annexations and unrestricted submarine warfare. After the defeat he founded the German People’s Party and came to accept the republic. Chancellor and foreign minister from August 1923, he ended passive resistance in the Ruhr, used the army to remove the Saxon and Thuringian governments that included Communists, and halted hyperinflation with the Rentenmark. Ousted by a no-confidence vote in November, he remained foreign minister until his death, shaping the Dawes Plan, the Locarno treaties and entry into the League of Nations, and shared the 1926 Nobel Peace Prize. He died of a stroke in 1929.

bio.en: Born in Salonica, he joined the Young Turk movement and made his name defending Gallipoli in the First World War. After the defeat he landed at Samsun in May 1919 to organise the national movement against occupation, and in 1920 convened the Grand National Assembly in Ankara. With gold and arms from the Bolshevik government he defeated the Greek army, and the Treaty of Lausanne recognised the victory. In these years the ethnic cleansing of Anatolia’s Armenians and Greeks was completed through massacres, deportations and population exchange. He abolished the sultanate in 1922 and in 1923 became the first president of the republic, pursuing secularising reforms and Turkification under one-party rule. He died in 1938.

bio.en: Born in Gelsenkirchen to a gendarmerie sergeant’s family, he trained as a teacher and was a military leader of the Red Ruhr Army during the Kapp Putsch of 1920. As a GRU agent and Comintern military adviser he co-organised the Guangzhou Uprising in China, and in the Spanish Civil War, as “Gomez”, he led the International Brigades. He returned to Germany in 1947, joined the SED, and in 1950 became the first Minister for State Security and a Politburo member, building up the Stasi. After the uprising of June 1953 he moved to replace Ulbricht with Herrnstadt, but once Ulbricht had Khrushchev’s backing he lost his ministry and all his posts in July and was expelled from the party. He worked as a translator, died in East Berlin in 1958 and was rehabilitated after 1990.

bio.en: A toolmaker from Berlin, he joined the SPD in 1910 and sat in the Prussian Landtag from 1928 to 1933. Under the Nazis he took part in a resistance group and was twice imprisoned. After the war he supported the forced merger of the SPD and KPD, sat on the SED’s Central Committee, and in October 1949 became the GDR’s first Minister of Justice. In the trial of the Gladow gang he had adult criminal law applied unlawfully so that a death sentence was possible. In an interview with Neues Deutschland on 30 June 1953 he said that members of the 17 June strike leadership would not be punished on mere suspicion; denounced as an “enemy of the state and the party”, he was dismissed, expelled and arrested, and sentenced to eight years. Released and pardoned in 1956, readmitted to the party in 1958, he died in 1973.

bio.en: Born in Münden in the Province of Hanover, he took part in the sailors’ revolt of 1918, joined the KPD in 1919 and led party military wings; he sat in the Reichstag in 1932–1933. In exile he organised the “Wollweber League” in 1936–1940, which carried out 21 known acts of sabotage against ships of fascist nations, and supplied arms to the Spanish Republicans. Back in Germany in 1946 he ran shipping administration. In July 1953, when Zaisser was removed and the Ministry for State Security was downgraded to a State Secretariat, he became its head, and in November 1955 Minister of State Security again. He clashed with Ulbricht and Honecker and sided with Schirdewan, resigned in 1957, and in 1958 was removed from the Central Committee for “factional activity”. He died in East Berlin in 1967.

bio.en: Born in Burg, the son of a Social Democratic worker, he worked as a tanner and left the SPD when it voted for war loans. He went through the USPD into the KPD and led its Magdeburg and East Prussia districts. Arrested in 1933, he escaped and went into exile, joining the National Committee for a Free Germany in the Soviet Union. He returned in 1945 with Anton Ackermann’s group and until 1946 was first secretary of the KPD in Saxony. From 1948 until his death he chaired the SED’s Central Party Control Commission, responsible for party discipline, and was a Politburo member and vice-president of the People’s Chamber. bio.en: The son of a hosier from Thalheim in Saxony, he joined the KPD in 1926 and attended the International Lenin School in Moscow. After underground work and exile under the Nazis he directed a political school of the International Brigades in the Spanish Civil War, and in Moscow ran the “Free Germany” radio station. In 1945 he led the KPD group sent to Saxony and drafted the party’s appeal of 11 June 1945. In 1946 he argued that socialism could be built in Germany without a preceding dictatorship of the proletariat, a “special German road to socialism” he had to recant after Tito’s break with Stalin in 1948. He served as deputy foreign minister and first head of the GDR’s foreign intelligence service, and in 1953 was stripped of all posts for supporting Zaisser. Gravely ill with cancer, he took his own life in 1973.

bio.en: Born in Kulm in West Prussia, he lost his right arm in the First World War and joined the SPD in 1918. As a member of the Württemberg Landtag and the Reichstag he fought the Nazis. Arrested in July 1933, he refused to sign a renunciation of political activity and spent ten years in concentration camps. In 1945 he rebuilt the party from Hanover, rejected the merger with the Communists urged by Otto Grotewohl in the Soviet zone, and called the KPD “red-painted Nazis”. Elected SPD chairman in 1946 and the Bundestag’s first leader of the opposition in 1949, he called for the nationalisation of heavy industry and a united Germany and opposed Adenauer’s integration with the West. He died in Bonn in 1952.

bio.en: A bookbinder from Hammelburg in Bavaria, he became a leader of the Catholic trade-union movement and was elected to the Reichstag for the Centre Party in 1933. He joined the resistance against the Nazis, was arrested by the Gestapo in 1938, and went into hiding after the 20 July 1944 plot. After the war he co-founded the CDU in the Soviet zone and became its co-chairman with Ernst Lemmer; as a Christian Socialist he called for the nationalisation of key industries. Critical of the Communists, he and Lemmer were removed as chairmen by the Soviet Military Administration in December 1947, and he moved to West Berlin. He opposed Adenauer’s Western integration in favour of a neutral, united Germany, and was minister for all-German affairs from 1949 to 1957. He died in Berlin in 1961.

bio.en: Born in Frohburg in Saxony, he worked as a journalist, moved through the left-liberal parties, helped found the German Democratic Party in 1918, and sat in the Weimar National Assembly and the Prussian Landtag. He joined the opposition after 1933 and went into hiding after the 1944 attempt on Hitler’s life. In 1945 he co-founded the CDU in the Soviet zone; when the Soviet authorities deposed Jakob Kaiser and Ernst Lemmer in 1947 he became acting chairman, and chairman in 1948. As a co-chairman of the German People’s Council he took part in drafting the GDR constitution, and in 1949 became deputy prime minister and head of the Church Office. A loyal supporter of the SED regime, he pushed out CDU members unwilling to follow the Communists. He died in 1957.

bio.en: An economist trained in Leningrad, he joined the Communist Party in 1927. He went into hiding during the Great Terror, and his parents were repressed. In the war he headed the 7th department of several fronts’ political administrations. From October 1945 to September 1949 he headed the Propaganda (later Information) Administration of the Soviet Military Administration in Germany; fluent in German, he strongly backed Walter Ulbricht. He pushed the 1946 merger of the KPD and SPD and from 1948 the development of a separate state on Soviet lines. He fell from favour as it became clear that Stalin did not support his and Ulbricht’s plans for rapid socialisation, and in 1949, after accusations from counter-intelligence, he was recalled. He later taught economics at Leningrad University.

bio.ko: 보스니아 서부의 가난한 세르비아계 농가에서 태어나 사라예보에서 공부했고, 1911년 오스트리아 지배에서 보스니아를 해방하고 남슬라브를 통일하려는 비밀 결사 청년 보스니아에 들어갔다. 반오스트리아 시위로 퇴학당해 베오그라드로 갔다. 세르비아 비밀 결사 흑수단에게 무기와 훈련을 받아, 1914년 6월 28일 사라예보에서 황위 계승자 프란츠 페르디난트 대공과 아내 조피를 권총으로 쏘아 죽였다. 이 암살이 7월 위기와 1차 세계대전으로 이어졌다. 재판에서 자신을 유고슬라비아 민족주의자라 밝혔고, 스무 살이 안 되어 사형을 면하고 징역 20년을 받았다. 1918년 테레지엔슈타트 요새 감옥에서 결핵으로 죽었다.
bio.en: Born to a poor Serb farming family in western Bosnia, he studied in Sarajevo and in 1911 joined Young Bosnia, a secret society seeking to free Bosnia from Austrian rule and unite the South Slavs. Expelled from school after anti-Austrian demonstrations, he went to Belgrade. Armed and trained through the Serbian secret society the Black Hand, on 28 June 1914 in Sarajevo he shot dead the heir to the throne, Archduke Franz Ferdinand, and his wife Sophie. The assassination set off the July Crisis and the First World War. At his trial he declared himself a Yugoslav nationalist; too young for the death penalty, he received twenty years. He died of tuberculosis in the prison of the Theresienstadt fortress in 1918.

bio.ko: 그라츠에서 프란츠 요제프 황제의 동생 카를 루트비히 대공의 맏아들로 태어났다. 1889년 루돌프 황태자가 자살하고 1896년 아버지가 죽자 황위 계승자가 되었다. 조피 호테크와의 귀천상혼은 자녀의 계승권을 포기한 뒤에야 허락되었다. 군에 큰 영향력을 행사했고 1913년 전군 총감이 되었다. 성직주의와 반민주주의, 반헝가리주의를 신념으로 삼았으며, 제국 안 슬라브 민족들의 자치 확대를 주장하는 한편 세르비아에 대해서는 러시아와의 충돌을 경계해 신중론을 폈다. 1914년 6월 28일 사라예보에서 아내와 함께 가브릴로 프린치프에게 암살되었고, 이 사건이 7월 위기와 전쟁으로 이어졌다.
bio.en: Born in Graz, the eldest son of Archduke Karl Ludwig, the younger brother of Emperor Franz Joseph, he became heir presumptive after Crown Prince Rudolf’s suicide in 1889 and his father’s death in 1896. His morganatic marriage to Sophie Chotek was allowed only after he renounced his descendants’ rights to the throne. He exerted great influence over the armed forces and in 1913 became their inspector general. Clericalism, anti-democratic views and anti-Hungarianism were the cornerstones of his politics; he advocated more autonomy for the empire’s Slav peoples, but urged caution towards Serbia for fear of conflict with Russia. On 28 June 1914 he and his wife were assassinated in Sarajevo by Gavrilo Princip, setting off the July Crisis and the war.

bio.ko: 브란덴부르크주 퀴스트린에서 법률가의 아들로 태어났다. 1897~1916년 제국해군청 장관으로 작은 제국 해군을 영국 해군을 위협할 세계적 해군으로 키웠다. 「위험 이론」에 따른 1898~1912년 함대법으로 독일 해군은 세계 2위가 되었지만, 값비싼 건함 경쟁을 부르고 영국을 프랑스 쪽으로 더 가깝게 밀었다. 그는 해군력이 사회민주당에 대한 「진정제」가 되리라 보았다. 전쟁 중 대양함대가 영국의 해상 봉쇄를 깨지 못하자 무제한 잠수함전을 거세게 주장했고, 1916년 3월 사임했다. 1917년 협상에 의한 강화에 반대하는 극우 조국당을 함께 세워 의장이 되었고, 전후 독일국가인민당 의원을 지냈다. 1930년 죽었다.
bio.en: Born in Küstrin in Brandenburg, the son of a lawyer, he was State Secretary of the Imperial Naval Office from 1897 to 1916 and turned the modest Imperial Navy into a world-class force that could threaten the Royal Navy. The Fleet Acts of 1898–1912, built on his “risk theory”, gave Germany the second-largest navy in the world, but started a costly naval arms race and pushed Britain closer to France. He saw sea power as a “palliative against” the Social Democrats. When the High Seas Fleet could not break Britain’s blockade, he became an outspoken advocate of unrestricted submarine warfare, and resigned in March 1916. In 1917 he co-founded and chaired the far-right Fatherland Party, which opposed a negotiated peace, and after the war sat in the Reichstag for the German National People’s Party. He died in 1930.

epithet.en: French commander-in-chief whose failed offensive of 1917 brought on the army mutinies and his dismissal

bio.ko: 코레즈의 튈에서 프랑스인 아버지와 영국인 개신교도 어머니 사이에서 태어나 포병 장교가 되었고, 의화단 진압에도 참전했다. 1916년 5월 베르됭에서 페탱의 뒤를 이어 제2군 사령관이 되어 반격을 이끌었으나, 병사들의 목숨을 낭비했다는 비난을 받았다. 1916년 12월 서부전선 프랑스군 총사령관이 되었고, 1917년 4월 16일 슈맹 데 담에서 결정적 돌파를 장담하며 니벨 공세를 열었다. 예상한 1만 명과 달리 열흘 만에 13만 4천 명의 사상자를 내고도 공격을 이어 갔으나 돌파에 실패했다. 프랑스군 절반가량이 항명에 휩싸였고, 5월 15일 페탱에게 자리를 넘겼다. 북아프리카 사령관으로 밀려났고 1924년 죽었다.
bio.en: Born in Tulle, Corrèze, to a French father and an English Protestant mother, he became an artillery officer and served in the Boxer Rebellion. In May 1916 he succeeded Pétain in command of the Second Army at Verdun and led the counter-offensives, but was accused of wasting French lives. Made commander-in-chief on the Western Front in December 1916, he opened the Nivelle Offensive at the Chemin des Dames on 16 April 1917, promising a decisive breakthrough. Casualties reached 134,000 in ten days against the 10,000 he had predicted, yet he pressed on without breaking through. A mutiny spread through roughly half the French Army, and on 15 May he was replaced by Pétain. He was sent off to command in North Africa and died in 1924.

bio.ko: 피에몬테에서 장군의 아들로 태어나 포병 장교가 되었고, 엄격한 군기와 공세 교리로 이름이 났다. 1914~1917년 이탈리아군 참모총장으로 이손초강을 따라 공세를 거듭했다. 고리치아 점령 같은 성과도 있었으나 「소모전만이 전쟁을 끝낸다」며 큰 희생을 감수했다. 장교 217명을 해임하고 후퇴한 부대의 장교를 즉결 처형하게 했으며, 그의 휘하에서 약 750명이 처형되어 1차 세계대전 군대 가운데 가장 많았다. 1917년 10월 카포레토에서 독일-오스트리아군에 대패해 27만 5천 명이 포로가 되었고, 11월 7일 해임되었다. 1924년 무솔리니 정권 아래 원수가 되었고 1928년 죽었다.
bio.en: Born in Piedmont, the son of a general, he became an artillery officer known for strict discipline and the doctrine of the offensive. As chief of staff of the Italian Army in 1914–1917 he launched offensive after offensive along the Isonzo. There were gains such as Gorizia, but he accepted huge losses, holding that the war could only end through the exhaustion of men and resources. He dismissed 217 officers and ordered the summary execution of officers whose units retreated; about 750 soldiers were executed under him, the most of any army in the war. After the disaster at Caporetto in October 1917, where 275,000 soldiers were captured, he was dismissed on 7 November. He was made a Marshal of Italy in 1924 under Mussolini and died in 1928.

bio.ko: 케임브리지에서 태어나 킹스 칼리지에서 수학을 공부했다. 1915년 재무부에 들어가 연합국 간 신용 조건을 설계했다. 파리 강화회의에서는 독일의 배상액을 지불 능력을 넘지 않게 하려 했으나 고위 협상에서 대부분 밀려났고, 조약에 실망해 재무부를 떠났다. 1919년 『평화의 경제적 귀결』로 조약의 해악을 예측해 국제적 명성을 얻었다. 대공황 속에서 유효수요가 경제활동 수준을 정한다고 보고 재정·통화 정책으로 불황에 맞설 것을 주장했으며, 1936년 『일반이론』을 냈다. 1944년 브레턴우즈 협상에서 영국 대표단을 이끌었으나 미국안에 밀렸다. 1946년 심장마비로 죽었다.
bio.en: Born in Cambridge, he studied mathematics at King’s College. Entering the Treasury in 1915, he designed the terms of credit between Britain and its continental allies. At the Paris Peace Conference he tried to keep Germany’s reparations within its capacity to pay but was largely excluded from the high-level talks, and the treaty’s outcome led to his resignation from the Treasury. The Economic Consequences of the Peace (1919), predicting the treaty’s damaging effects, made him internationally famous. In the Depression he argued that aggregate demand determined the level of economic activity and called for fiscal and monetary policy against slumps, publishing The General Theory in 1936. He led the British delegation at Bretton Woods in 1944, where the American plan largely prevailed. He died of heart attacks in 1946.

bio.ko: 튀링겐 줄의 관료 집안에서 태어나 법학을 공부했고, 재무부 관리로 1차 세계대전 초 독일의 식량 공급을 조직했다. 1917년 해운회사 함부르크-아메리카 노선에 들어가 사장이 되었다. 1922년 11월 의회 표결 없이 대통령령으로 바이마르 공화국 최초의 무당파 총리가 되어 「실무 내각」을 꾸렸다. 1923년 1월 프랑스·벨기에군이 루르를 점령하자 소극적 저항을 호소했고, 그 비용을 주로 돈을 찍어 대면서 초인플레이션이 시작되었다. 파업의 물결 속에 8월 사회민주당이 낸 불신임으로 물러났다. 1932년 히틀러의 경제 자문에 참여했고 1933년 1월 죽었다.
bio.en: Born to a civil servant’s family in Suhl, he studied law and, as a Treasury official, helped organise Germany’s food supply early in the First World War. In 1917 he joined the Hamburg America shipping line, which he went on to head. In November 1922 he was appointed chancellor by presidential decree without a Reichstag vote, the first Weimar chancellor who belonged to no party, and formed a “business ministry”. When French and Belgian troops occupied the Ruhr in January 1923 he called for passive resistance; paying for it, mostly by printing money, began the run-up to hyperinflation. Amid a wave of strikes his cabinet resigned in August in the face of a no-confidence vote initiated by the SPD. In 1932 he joined in advising Hitler on economics, and he died in January 1933.

bio.ko: 동프로이센 다르케멘에서 태어나 변호사 사무원으로 일하다 사무직 노동조합을 세웠고, 1908~1918년 자유노동조합 총위원회 부의장을 지냈다. 1912년 사회민주당 제국의회 의원이 되었고 1918년 10월 막스 폰 바덴 내각의 노동장관이 되었다. 1919년 6월 샤이데만이 베르사유 조약에 항의해 사임하자, 조약을 비판해 왔으면서도 후임 총리를 맡아 조약 비준을 이끌었다. 재정 개혁과 사회보험 확대를 펼쳤으나, 1920년 3월 카프 폭동 때 반란군과 협상한 일로 정부가 물러났다. 뒤에 부총리 겸 재무장관을 지냈고, 바르마트 부패 사건으로 1925년 의원직을 내놓았다. 1944년 베를린에서 죽었다.
bio.en: Born in Darkehmen in the Province of Prussia, he worked as a lawyer’s clerk, co-founded the office employees’ union and was second chairman of the General Commission of Trade Unions from 1908 to 1918. Elected to the Reichstag for the SPD in 1912, he became labour secretary in Max von Baden’s cabinet in October 1918. When Scheidemann resigned in protest at the Treaty of Versailles in June 1919, Bauer, until then a vocal critic of the treaty, succeeded him and got it through the National Assembly. His government carried out tax reform and extended social insurance, but was forced out in March 1920 over the negotiations conducted with the Kapp putschists. He was later vice-chancellor and treasury minister, and the Barmat corruption scandal cost him his seat in 1925. He died in Berlin in 1944.

epithet.en: Conservative viceroy of India and foreign secretary who gave his name to the Curzon Line and led the Allies at Lausanne

bio.ko: 더비셔의 귀족 집안에서 태어나 이튼과 옥스퍼드를 거쳐 1885년 하원에 들어갔고, 러시아의 인도 위협을 경고하는 여행기를 썼다. 1899~1905년 인도 총독으로 행정 개혁을 폈지만, 1905년 벵골 분할로 민족주의를 갈라놓으려 했다는 비판을 받았고 재임 중 대기근이 겹쳤다. 1차 세계대전 중 로이드 조지의 전시 내각에 들어갔고, 1919년 10월 외무장관이 되어 소련-폴란드 경계안인 커즌선에 이름을 남겼다. 세브르 조약을 설계했고, 1922년 로잔 회의에서 연합국 수석 협상자로 튀르키예의 국경을 정했다. 1923년 총리 자리를 놓쳤고 1925년 죽었다.
bio.en: Born into an aristocratic Derbyshire family and educated at Eton and Oxford, he entered Parliament in 1885 and wrote travel books warning of a Russian threat to India. As Viceroy of India from 1899 to 1905 he pursued administrative reform, but his 1905 partition of Bengal was criticised as an attempt to divide Bengali nationalism, and a major famine coincided with his tenure. In the First World War he served in Lloyd George’s war cabinet; appointed Foreign Secretary in October 1919, he gave his name to the proposed Soviet-Polish boundary, the Curzon Line. He designed the Treaty of Sèvres and, as chief Allied negotiator at Lausanne in 1922, settled the borders of Turkey. Passed over for prime minister in 1923, he died in 1925.

bio.ko: 스미르나에서 태어난 오스만 장교로, 독립전쟁에서 대국민의회군 참모총장과 서부전선 사령관으로 1·2차 이뇌뉘 전투를 이겼다. 1922~1923년 로잔 회의의 튀르키예 수석 협상자로 커즌에 맞서며 세브르 조약을 로잔 조약으로 대체했다. 아타튀르크 아래 오래 총리를 지내며 세속화 개혁을 집행했고, 셰이크 사이드 반란 뒤 쿠르드인의 튀르크화를 밀어붙였으며 데르심 학살의 책임자로도 꼽힌다. 1938년 2대 대통령이 되어 「국가 지도자」 칭호를 받았고, 2차 세계대전에서 무장 중립을 지켰다. 1950년 선거 패배로 평화적으로 정권을 넘겼다. 1973년 죽었다.
bio.en: Born in Smyrna, an Ottoman officer, he won the First and Second Battles of İnönü in the War of Independence as chief of the General Staff and commander of the Western Front. As Turkey’s chief negotiator at Lausanne in 1922–1923 he faced down Curzon and replaced the Treaty of Sèvres with the Treaty of Lausanne. As prime minister for most of Atatürk’s presidency he carried out the secularising reforms; after the Sheikh Said revolt he pushed the Turkification of the Kurds, and he is considered one of those responsible for the Dersim massacre. Elected second president in 1938, he took the title “National Chief” and kept Turkey in armed neutrality in the Second World War. After defeat in the 1950 election he handed over power peacefully. He died in 1973.
